assets/vo/s01-850e2878.mp3: Part two: how does AI actually use embeddings?
assets/vo/s02-789b4a23.mp3: Quick recap: an embedding model turns a word's meaning into a list of numbers.
assets/vo/s02-7f4aebd6.mp3: That whole list is the embedding.
assets/vo/s03-b25dc560.mp3: Squash all those numbers down to two, and each word gets a spot on a map.
assets/vo/s03-9385d5c4.mp3: Dog and puppy are neighbours. Pizza? Way over here.
assets/vo/s04-74beffc6.mp3: A computer can score how close two spots are.
assets/vo/s04-82932496.mp3: Dog and puppy: point eight. Dog and pizza: point three five.
assets/vo/s04-f2fabb38.mp3: Pizza isn't zero, because scores are fuzzy. What matters is which is closest.
assets/vo/s05-a1b6cbc6.mp3: That score has a name: cosine similarity.
assets/vo/s05-a627ccc8.mp3: Picture each embedding as an arrow. It measures the angle between two arrows.
assets/vo/s05-a15a325e.mp3: Dog and puppy: a small angle, so a high score.
assets/vo/s05-1bf8dd73.mp3: Dog and pizza: a wider angle, so a lower score.
assets/vo/s05-6891aee6.mp3: Pointing the same way scores one. At a right angle, zero.
assets/vo/s06-5599cb4f.mp3: Keyword search spots the word bike, and gets it wrong.
assets/vo/s06-9e01821b.mp3: Embedding search matches the meaning, and finds the fix.
assets/vo/s07-def10c97.mp3: Where do embeddings live? In a database.
assets/vo/s07-9ab39eb5.mp3: Take a team handbook and split it into chunks.
assets/vo/s07-199c6a83.mp3: Each row stores a chunk and its numbers.
assets/vo/s08-6c54de31.mp3: A vector database searches those numbers by closeness.
assets/vo/s08-f6efaf4d.mp3: Ask a question, and it becomes numbers too.
assets/vo/s08-dcab77e0.mp3: The database finds the nearest chunk.
assets/vo/s09-e68ed91f.mp3: That chunk goes to Claude, along with your question.
assets/vo/s09-342a6faa.mp3: So Claude answers from the right page.
